activity_description: Give the child a basin or patch of sand with cups, spoons and a funnel. Let them scoop, pour, fill and empty. Talk about full and empty as they play, and wash hands afterwards.
cultural_relevance: A funnel cut from a plastic bottle and kitchen spoons make good sand toys.

developmental_goal: Help the child draw and explore a soft texture with their fingers
required_materials: Shaving cream or soap foam; a tray or table
activity_description: Spread shaving cream or thick soap foam on a tray and let the child draw lines, circles and shapes with their finger. Smooth it over and start again. Keep it away from their eyes.
cultural_relevance: Thick foam from bar soap is a low-cost alternative.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore loud and quiet sounds through music
required_materials: Drums, shakers or pots and spoons
activity_description: Play homemade instruments together and take turns playing loudly and quietly, fast and slowly. Ask the child to copy your rhythm, then copy theirs. Name each sound: loud, quiet, fast, slow.
cultural_relevance: A drum made from a tin with a plastic lid and bottle shakers make a home band.

developmental_goal: Help the child explore pouring, filling and emptying water
required_materials: A basin of water; cups and containers of different sizes
activity_description: Set out a basin of water with cups and containers of different sizes. Let the child pour from one to another and see which holds more. Talk about full, empty, more and less. Stay with them near water.
cultural_relevance: Plastic cups, jugs and bottles from the kitchen are all you need.

activity_name: Barefoot on Grass, Sand and Soil
developmental_goal: Help the child get used to the feel of grass, sand and soil
activity_description: In a safe, clean area, let the child walk barefoot on grass, sand and soil. Talk about how each one feels. Some children need several tries before they enjoy new textures, so keep offering it gently.
cultural_relevance: The compound, shamba edges or a school field offer a range of surfaces.

developmental_goal: Help the child notice new sights and sounds on trips
activity_description: On outings such as a bus or matatu ride, a walk or a market visit, point out new sights, sounds and smells. Ask the child what they can see and hear. Encourage their questions and curiosity.
cultural_relevance: Market days and matatu rides are full of colour and sound.

activity_name: Sharing and Taking Turns with Friends
developmental_goal: Help the child learn to share, take turns and solve conflicts with words
activity_description: When the child plays with other children, stay close and show them how to share and take turns. If there is a conflict, help them use words: 'Can I have a turn?' Praise kind play.
cultural_relevance: Playing with neighbours' and cousins' children gives regular practice.

developmental_goal: Help the child name feelings and learn ways to calm down
activity_description: Help the child put words to feelings: 'You're angry because the tower fell.' Teach simple calming steps, such as taking deep breaths, hugging a soft toy or going to a quiet spot. Practise them when the child is calm too.
cultural_relevance: Name feelings in the family's language as well as English.

developmental_goal: Help the child understand a few clear family rules
activity_description: Choose a few simple, clear rules, such as 'We walk inside' and 'We are gentle with others'. Explain them in simple words, gently redirect when they are broken, and praise the child when they follow them.
cultural_relevance: Agree the rules with all carers so they are the same everywhere.

developmental_goal: Help the child feel ready for new places and people
activity_description: Before a new experience, such as starting day care or visiting the clinic, use stories or pretend play to show what will happen. Play doctor or school with toys and talk about who they will meet.
cultural_relevance: Helpful before starting ECDE, visiting relatives or going to the clinic.
